# Adjudication Task — Chapter 949

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃949화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|모든 일에는 전조(前兆)가 있다.
  6|
  7|지진이 가까워지면 땅 울림과 함께 무수한 날짐승들이 일제히 날아오르고, 태풍이 들이닥치기 전에는 새털구름이 하늘을 가득 메우는 것처럼.
  8|
  9|천벌이나 다름없는 자연재해조차 그럴진대, 한낱 인간이 벌이는 일이라면 더 무슨 말이 필요할까.
 10|
 11|지금으로부터 불과 며칠 전, 몇몇 이들은 초원에서 전해지는 심상치 않은 징조를 느낄 수 있었다.
 12|
 13|그것도 아주 또렷하면서도 분명하게.
 14|
 15|‘유목민들이. 아니, 초원 전체가 움직이고 있다.’
 16|
 17|옅은 어둠이 내리깔린 드넓은 대전(大殿) 내부. 장대한 체구의 사내는 말 없이 눈앞에 놓인 지도를 응시했다.
 18|
 19|장정 서넛을 합친 것만큼이나 커다란 지도에는 대륙 전체의 지형과 지명으로 빼곡하게 채워져 있었으나, 그의 시선은 오직 한곳에 못 박혀 있을 뿐이었다.
 20|
 21|산서(山西).
 22|
 23|사내가 일평생을 나고 자란 고향이자, 선조들이 지켜온 땅.
 24|
 25|지금으로부터 삼백여 년 전, 천하를 피로 물들이던 전란의 끄트머리에서 한 사람이 이 땅에 다다랐다.
 26|
 27|성은 진가요, 이름은 무량이라.
 28|
 29|그는 본래 환영받지 못하는 이방인이었으나, 태원(太原)에 이르러 주춧돌을 내려놓고 깃발을 세우니 그것이 곧 태원진가의 시작이었다.
 30|
 31|‘그분께서도 모르셨겠지. 본가가 이토록 장구한 세월을 이겨 낼 수 있으리라고는.’
 32|
 33|삼백여 년.
 34|
 35|아득한 세월이다.
 36|
 37|보는 이로 하여금 탄성을 자아내던 화려한 꽃도, 모두를 압도시킬 만큼 높고 크던 거목(巨木)도 반복되는 겨울과 시간 앞에서 쓰러졌다.
 38|
 39|그러나 변방의 잡초는, 태원진가는 지금까지도 이 땅을 지키고 있다.
 40|
 41|흐드러지게 피었다가, 꺾이고, 부서지고, 다시 일어나며.
 42|
 43|“흥망성쇠(興亡盛衰)라.”
 44|
 45|나직하게 뇌까린 사내, 진위경은 천천히 말을 이었다.
 46|
 47|“본가의 흥(興)은 이미 오래전에 지났고, 망(亡)은 간신히 피할 수 있었지. 하여 이제는 틀림없이 성(盛)할 일만 남았다고 생각했는데…….”
 48|
 49|진위경은 웃었다. 씁쓸하게.
 50|
 51|“헛다리 한 번 제대로 짚었군. 자네도 그리 생각하지 않나?”
 52|
 53|듣는 이 하나 없는 넋두리도, 혼잣말도 아니다.
 54|
 55|철탑처럼 무겁고 호수처럼 고요하게 자신의 자리를 지키고 있던 위팽이 입을 열었다.
 56|
 57|“지금 주군의 모습을 보고 있자니, 문득 옛 생각이 나는군요.”
 58|
 59|“옛 생각?”
 60|
 61|“사실 옛날이라고 부를 만큼 오래된 일은 아닙니다. 고작 이 년 전이니까요.”
 62|
 63|“항산검문(恒山劍門)…….”
 64|
 65|“맞습니다. 그때도 주군께서는 이런 모습이셨죠.”
 66|
 67|위팽은 귀검(鬼劍)이라는 별호처럼 서늘한 목소리로 말을 이었다.
 68|
 69|“싸움은 시작도 안 했습니다. 검을 뽑기도 전에 내려놓으실 생각이십니까?”
 70|
 71|“그리 보이나?”
 72|
 73|“그렇게 보입니다. 지금 제 눈에는.”
 74|
 75|가장 가까운 충복의 단호한 대답에 진위경은 입술을 깨물었다.
 76|
 77|즉각 부정하지 못하는 스스로의 모습이 부끄러워서.
 78|
 79|그와 더불어 찰나의 오기로나마 결정을 내리지 못하게 만드는 현실이 암담해서.
 80|
 81|“나는…… 본가의 소가주일세. 짧은 말 몇 마디, 사소한 행동 하나에 수많은 목숨이 걸려 있어.”
 82|
 83|비단 태원진가뿐만이 아니다.
 84|
 85|산서 무림 전체가 진위경의 의지에 따라 움직인다.
 86|
 87|태원진가는 명실상부한 산서성의 패자이며, 그는 사실상 가주나 다름없으니까.
 88|
 89|그리고 지금 이 순간에도 수만에 달하는 인마(人馬)의 파도는 이 땅을 향해 짓쳐 들고 있다.
 90|
 91|“이미 산서성부를 통해 대동(大同)과 산음(山陰) 일대의 백성들을 대피시키라는 서한을 보냈네. 애꿎은 피해를 최대한 막아야 할 테니.”
 92|
 93|대동과 산음은 초원과 가장 가까이에 인접한 현읍(縣邑).
 94|
 95|국경을 넘어선 초원의 군세가 가장 먼저 짓밟고 지나갈 곳이기도 했다.
 96|
 97|“항산검문 역시 마찬가지야. 물러서기에는 아직 늦지 않았네. 그것만이 멸문(滅門)을 피할 유일한 방법이지.”
 98|
 99|“이 문주가 과연 그 제안을 받아들이리라 생각하십니까?”
100|
101|“제안이 아닐세. 이건 명령이야.”
102|
103|진위경은 가라앉은 목소리로 말을 이었다.
104|
105|“다른 선택지가 없으니 지금쯤이면 그녀도 현실을 받아들였겠지.”
106|
107|지난 이 년간, 태원진가의 깃발 아래에 몸을 의탁한 항산검문도 눈부신 성장을 이루었다.
108|
109|여인의 몸으로 새롭게 문주가 된 이소월은 모두가 생각했던 것 이상으로 뛰어난 수완가였다.
110|
111|전대 문주이자 부친이었던 혈랑검 이천백이 공포와 무력으로 항산검문을 세웠다면, 그녀는 특유의 영민함과 지도력으로 몰락 직전의 위기에 처해 있던 문파를 재건시켰다.
112|
113|세간의 이목을 집중시킬 정도로.
114|
115|그러나 제아무리 성장에 성장을 거듭했다 하더라도, 코앞에 닥친 위기를 헤쳐 나갈 수는 없을 것이 분명했다.
116|
117|“삼만.”
118|
119|진위경이 무거운 눈빛으로 위팽을 응시했다.
120|
121|“놈들이 산서성에 이를 때쯤이면 삼만으로 불어나 있을 걸세.”
122|
123|지난 며칠 간의 시간은 잔인하리만치 빠르게 흘렀다.
124|
125|초원 곳곳에 흩어져 있던 유목민들이 집결하고 있다는 급보를 접한 어느 날, 초원의 교역로에 자리 잡은 여러 표국과 상단이 사라졌다.
126|
127|물론 그들의 생사도, 흉수도 뻔했다.
128|
129|“놈들의 목적은 분명하네. 뒤에 누가 있는지도.”
130|
131|진위경은 테무르와 칭겐에 대해 잘 알고 있었다.
132|
133|두 사람이 초원의 실력자로 급부상할 수 있었던 결정적인 이유 중 하나는, 태원진가의 지원이 있었기 때문이기도 했다.
134|
135|“테무르는 강하지만 지극히 단순하고, 칭겐은 심계가 깊고 신중하나 지닌바 그릇이 작지. 절대로 이런 짓을 벌일 위인들이 아니야. 그럴 만한 힘도 없고.”
136|
137|초원의 유목민들이 활과 돌격창으로 대륙을 질타했던 시대는 이미 오래전에 저물었다.
138|
139|그들이 세운 제국은 흔적도 없이 사라졌고, 광활하나 황량한 들판으로 내쫓긴 유목민들은 동족끼리의 반목과 쇠퇴를 거듭했다.
140|
141|“그들의 힘은 익히 입증된 바가 있네. 하지만 그 정도로는 중원을 넘보기에는 아직 부족해.”
142|
143|어느덧 칸이라 불리게 된 테무르와 칭겐도 결국 초원의 여러 대족장(大族長) 중 한 사람에 불과하다.
144|
145|반면 중원은 어떠한가.
146|
147|각 성마다 적게는 수천에서, 많게는 일만이 넘어가는 대국의 병사와 저력 있는 무림 문파가 존재한다.
148|
149|분열된 초원.
150|
151|단결된 중원.
152|
153|이 사이에는 너무나도 깊고 넓은 간격이 있다.
154|
155|유목민들이 선조들의 위업을 이어 천하를 지배할 날은 두 번 다시 오지 않을 것이다.
156|
157|또 다른 거대한 힘이 개입하지 않는 한은.
158|
159|“내가 두려워하는 것은 삼만의 유목민들이 아닐세.”
160|
161|진위경은 앞에 놓인 커다란 지도를 노려보았다.
162|
163|마치 이 빼곡한 그림과 글자 어디에선가, 숨어 있던 무언가가 튀어나오기만을 기다리는 듯이.
164|
165|“암천. 아직 드러나지 않은 놈들의 힘이, 나는 두렵네.”
166|
167|지난 이 년간 태원진가는 늘 승승장구해 왔다.
168|
169|그러나 축하와 환호의 나날 속에서, 진위경은 밤마다 찾아오는 끔찍한 악몽에 몸부림쳤다.
170|
171|죽은 자들이 나오는 악몽을.
172|
173|
174|
175|‘죽여라!’
176|
177|‘한 걸음도 물러서지 마라!’
178|
179|
180|
181|차차차창!
182|
183|팔천협(八天峽).
184|
185|적과 아군, 그리고 배신자들이 뒤엉켜 서로를 향해 짐승처럼 달려들던 피의 협곡에서 진위경은 매일 밤을 헤매었다.
186|
187|‘소가주님. 괜찮으십…… 커헉!’
188|
189|언제나 웃으며 인사를 건네던 가솔이 피를 흩뿌리며 쓰러지는 것을 보았고.
190|
191|‘사, 살려 주시오. 제발. 제발.’
192|
193|또 다른 적을 상대하기 위해 눈을 부릅뜬 채 죽어 가는 항산검문의 무인을 지나쳤으며.
194|
195|‘네놈이, 태원진가가 우리에게 무슨 짓을 했는지 아느냐!’
196|
197|수십여 년의 기다림 끝에 비로소 숨겨 두었던 칼을 빼 든 배신자들과 맞닥트렸다.
198|
199|그들과 쉴 새 없이 검을 섞고, 마침내 쓰러트리고, 한 사람과 마주했다.
200|
201|‘주위를 둘러보아라. 처참하게 죽어 가는 저들을 보며 무슨 생각이 드느냐?’
202|
203|핏물에 젖어 붉게 물든 수염.
204|
205|메마른 눈빛과 목소리.
206|
207|분명 오래전 죽었을 대장로는, 서늘한 숨결과 함께 자신의 핏줄을 향해 말하고 있었다.
208|
209|‘네가 조금 더 신중했더라면. 영민했더라면……. 오늘 같은 참극을 막을 수 있지 않았을까?’
210|
211|기억에는 없는 말이다.
212|
213|당연했다.
214|
215|그것은 진위경이 스스로에게 던지는 물음이었으니까.
216|
217|진위경은 알고 있었다.
218|
219|악몽 속의 대장로도, 그가 뱉은 모든 말도 결국 진위경 자신으로부터 비롯된 것이라는 사실을.
220|
221|하지만 그 사실을 알고 있음에도, 악몽은 끊이질 않고 반복되었다.
222|
223|지금 이 순간에도.
224|
225|“주군.”
226|
227|불현듯 귓가를 파고드는 위팽의 목소리에, 진위경은 지금 막 잠에서 깬 사람처럼 천천히 눈을 깜빡였다.
228|
229|그리고 어느덧 자신의 몸이 식은땀으로 축축하게 젖어 있다는 것을 깨달았다.
230|
231|“……제기랄. 꼬락서니하고는.”
232|
233|진위경은 외마디 욕설과 함께 실소를 터트렸다.
234|
235|우습기 짝이 없었다.
236|
237|비에 젖은 생쥐처럼 벌벌 떨고 있는 자신의 모습이.
238|
239|사방에서 조여 오는 중압감에 숨 쉬는 것조차 버거워하는 이 한심한 놈의 손에 산서 무림. 아니, 산서성 전체의 명운(命運)이 달렸다는 것이.
240|
241|그나마 한 줄기 위안이 되는 것은, 오랜 시간을 함께한 이가 곁에 있다는 사실뿐이었다.
242|
243|“속하가 한 말씀 드려도 되겠습니까.”
244|
245|잠시 내려앉은 침묵 속에서 울려 퍼지는 목소리.
246|
247|위팽은 진위경의 대답을 기다리지 않고 말을 이었다.
248|
249|“분명 적들은 강합니다. 삼만의 유목민에 아직 드러나지 않은 암천의 전력까지 더해진다면……. 주군의 판단대로 돌이킬 수 없는 일이 벌어질지도 모르지요.”
250|
251|“관부와 힘을 합쳐도 승산을 장담하기 어렵네. 지원군이 없는 한, 산서성의 전력을 총동원하여 쏟아부어도 감당할 수 없어.”
252|
253|진위경이 씁쓸하게 덧붙였다.
254|
255|“설령 천운이 닿아 지원군이 제때 도착하더라도, 병력이며 규모가 턱없이 부족하겠지. 당연한 일이야. 나로서도 같은 입장이라면 결코 가문을 비울 수 없을 테니까.”
256|
257|성동격서(聲東擊西).
258|
259|광활하기 그지없는 초원은 산서성은 물론 요녕, 하북, 섬서에까지 맞닿아 있다.
260|
261|산서성을 향해 남하하던 대군세가 말머리를 비트는 순간, 지원군을 파병한 문파와 가문은 새로운 표적이 된다.
262|

One day, urgent word had arrived that nomads scattered across the grasslands were gathering. Then several Escort Bureaus and merchant houses along the grassland trade routes had disappeared.

[P60]
Their fate was obvious. So were the culprits.

[P61]
“Their aim is clear. So is who’s behind them.”

[P62]
Jin Wikyung knew Temur and Chinggen well. Support from the Jin Family of Taiyuan had been one of the chief reasons the two men had risen so quickly to power on the grasslands.

[P63]
“Temur is strong, but utterly simple. Chinggen is calculating and cautious, but his ambitions are too small. Neither would ever attempt something like this. They don’t have the strength for it, either.”

[P64]
The age when grassland nomads had thundered across the continent with bows and lances was long gone.

[P65]
The empire they had built had vanished without a trace. Driven onto vast but desolate plains, the nomads had feuded among themselves and dwindled.

[P66]
“Their strength has been proven. But it still isn’t enough to threaten the Central Plains.”

[P67]
Temur and Chinggen might now be called khans, but each was only one of the grasslands’ many Great Chieftains.

[P68]
And the Central Plains?

[P69]
Every province had thousands—sometimes more than ten thousand—soldiers of the Great Nation, along with powerful Murim sects.

[P70]
The divided grasslands. The united Central Plains.

[P71]
The gulf between them was too deep and wide.

[P72]
The nomads would never again follow their ancestors’ path to rule the world.

[P73]
Not unless another great power intervened.

[P74]
“It isn’t thirty thousand nomads I’m afraid of.”

[P75]
Jin Wikyung glared at the enormous map, as though waiting for something hidden among its dense lines and characters to spring out.

[P76]
“Dark Heaven. I’m afraid of the strength they haven’t shown us yet.”

[P77]
For the past two years, the Jin Family of Taiyuan had gone from strength to strength.

[P78]
But through all the celebrations and cheers, Jin Wikyung had suffered a terrible nightmare every night.

[P79]
A nightmare filled with the dead.

[P80]
“Kill them!”

[P81]
“Don’t retreat a single step!”

[P82]
Clang! Clang! Clang!

[P83]
Eight Spring Gorge.

[P84]
Every night, Jin Wikyung wandered that bloody gorge, where enemies, allies, and traitors had charged at one another like beasts.

[P85]
“Lesser Family Head, are you all ri—ack!”

[P86]
He watched a family retainer who had always greeted him with a smile collapse in a spray of blood.

[P87]
“P-Please, spare me. Please. Please.”

[P88]
He passed a dying Mount Heng Sword Sect martial artist, eyes wide open, on his way to face another enemy.

[P89]
“Do you know what you and the Jin Family of Taiyuan did to us?!”

[P90]
He faced the traitors who had finally drawn the blades they had kept hidden for decades.

[P91]
He crossed swords with them without pause until, at last, he brought them down and stood before one man.

[P92]
“Look around you. What do you think when you see them dying like that?”

[P93]
A beard stained red with blood.

[P94]
A dry gaze. A dry voice.

[P95]
The Head Elder, who had surely died long ago, spoke to his own blood kin, his breath cold.

[P96]
“If you had been a little more careful. A little wiser…could you have prevented a tragedy like this?”

[P97]
Jin Wikyung had no memory of those words.

[P98]
Of course he didn’t.

[P99]
They were questions he asked himself.

[P100]
He knew the Head Elder in his nightmare—and every word the man spoke—came from within him.

[P101]
Even knowing that, he dreamed it again and again.

[P102]
Even now.

[P103]
“My lord.”

[P104]
Wipeng’s voice suddenly reached him. Jin Wikyung blinked slowly, like a man waking from sleep, and realized his body was damp with cold sweat.

[P105]
“…Damn it. Look at the state of me.”

[P106]
He gave a short, humorless laugh.

[P107]
It was ridiculous. He was trembling like a drenched rat.

[P108]
And the fate of Shanxi Murim—no, of all Shanxi Province—rested in the hands of this pathetic man, who could barely breathe beneath the pressure closing in on him.

[P109]
His one small comfort was that someone who had stood beside him for so long was still there.

[P110]
“May I say something, my lord?”

[P111]
Wipeng’s voice broke the brief silence. He continued without waiting for an answer.

[P112]
“The enemy is strong. If Dark Heaven’s hidden forces join thirty thousand nomads…you may be right. What happens then may be beyond undoing.”

[P113]
“Even with the government’s help, we can’t be sure we’d win. Without reinforcements, we couldn’t hold them off with every force Shanxi Province can muster.”

[P114]
Jin Wikyung added bitterly, “Even if we’re lucky enough to get reinforcements in time, there won’t be nearly enough. Of course there won’t. In their place, I couldn’t leave my family unprotected either.”

[P115]
A feint to the east, a strike in the west.

[P116]
The vast grasslands bordered not only Shanxi Province, but Liaoning, Hebei, and Shaanxi as well. The moment the army marching south toward Shanxi turned its horses elsewhere, the sects and families that had sent reinforcements would become its new targets.

[P117]
And while Dark Heaven possessed the strange dark art known as the Moving Formation, no one could easily leave their sect or family undefended.

[P118]
They had people to protect, too.

[P119]
“I intend to abandon Shanxi and head for Henan. As long as our people survive, our family won’t disappear.”

[P120]
This was neither the best choice nor the second-best.

[P121]
It was the lesser evil, chosen to avert the worst.

[P122]
Wipeng understood Jin Wikyung’s desire to prevent so many deaths.

[P123]
“If that is your command, my lord, I will obey.”

[P124]
“Wipeng, you…”

[P125]
“But my lord, do you remember?”

[P126]
Wipeng spoke calmly.

[P127]
“Two years ago, someone said that once you start retreating, you’ll keep backing away until you trip over a rock and fall.”

[P128]
“…!”

[P129]
“I know how strong the enemy is. And I know why you’ve made this decision. But…”

[P130]
Wipeng drew a deep breath and clasped his hands in salute to the lord he trusted and followed.

[P131]
“Our Jin Family of Taiyuan has grown stronger. No—Shanxi Murim has grown stronger.”

[P132]
He turned without hesitation and opened the tightly shut door.

[P133]
Swish.

[P134]
Jin Wikyung saw them then.

[P135]
Beyond the slowly opening door, countless people waited, armed and ready.

[P136]
Familiar faces stood at their head.

[P137]
“Lee Seowol of the Mount Heng Sword Sect. I’ve come to fight the foreign enemy.”

[P138]
Clang! Clang! Clang!

[P139]
Lee Seowol stood in martial attire. Behind her, three hundred Mount Heng Sword Sect martial artists drew their weapons and drove them deep into the ground.

[P140]
“Sect Leader Lee. What is all this…?”

[P141]
Jin Wikyung couldn’t finish.

[P142]
He had spotted the dozens of Sect Leaders and Family Heads who had sworn allegiance beneath the Jin Family of Taiyuan’s banner two years ago. Each stood armed, eyes cold.

[P143]
And among them was someone who had just appeared.

[P144]
“What’s got you so worried?”

[P145]
The voice was rough and awkward, as if the young man had forgotten how to speak.

[P146]
Dressed in rags, he smiled at Jin Wikyung. His cheeks were gaunt enough to make the smile stand out.

[P147]
“Hyung.”

[P148]
“…!”

[P149]
His younger brother had finally emerged into the world after a long seclusion. At the sight of him, Jin Wikyung closed his eyes, unable to contain the emotion rising within him.

[P150]
And in that instant of darkness, he recalled the voice of his youngest brother, absent from this room. The words Wipeng had repeated only moments ago.

[P151]
*Once you start retreating, you’ll keep backing away until you trip over a rock and fall.*

[P152]
Jin Wikyung couldn’t be sure which choice was right.

[P153]
But he knew which way he had to go.

[P154]
Step.

[P155]
He walked toward the people waiting for the Lesser Family Head of the Jin Family of Taiyuan.

[P156]
Toward the dark future from which the smell of blood was already drifting.

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.
